    Dating

    Due date and gestational age from the crown-rump length, fetal biometry, the IVF transfer date or the binocular distance, and a due date calculator. Choose the one you need.

    Dating scan

    1. Plane. Sagittal view of the fetus, transabdominal or transvaginal (ISUOG 2023). Fetus horizontal on the screen, so that the line from crown to rump is at about 90° to the beam. Image magnified to fill most of the width of the screen. Daya 1993 scanned transvaginally or transabdominally. Robinson 1975 made serial parallel scans across the sac until the longest length of the fetal echoes was found.
    2. Landmarks. The end points of the crown and the rump, both clearly seen. Fetus in a neutral position, neither flexed nor hyperextended (ISUOG 2023); the neck neutral (SOGC 388).
    3. Calipers. Along the longest straight line from the top of the head to the rump, on the end points of the crown and the rump (ISUOG 2023); from the outer margin of the head to the rump (SOGC 388). Use the best CRL or the average of several good ones (SOGC 388). Daya 1993: on the frozen image, on the outer margins of the head and trunk, along the longest axis with the fetus extended where possible; average of two to three measurements. Robinson 1975: the longest length of the fetal echoes, measured on a Polaroid photograph with the screen graticule as the rule.
    4. Result. Gestational age and due date from the chart chosen, with its 95% range: about ±5 days with Daya 1993, and ±4.7 days for one measurement with Robinson 1975 (±2.7 days for the average of three). Ideally use CRL from 10 mm (about 7 weeks), and up to 84 mm; above 84 mm, date from the BPD. With more than one first-trimester scan, use the earliest with a CRL of at least 10 mm (SOGC 388). ISUOG 2023 uses the best-quality CRL between 45 and 84 mm, and uses the CRL for dating in all pregnancies except those conceived by IVF. When the conception date is known, as with timed fertilization in assisted reproduction, the EDD is calculated from the fertilization date (SOGC 388); after IVF, it is assigned from the embryo age and the transfer date (Committee Opinion 700).
    5. Pitfalls. Do not date from the mean sac diameter once a CRL can be measured, and do not average the two (SOGC 388). Below 10 mm the very early fetus can be hard to see clearly, and the measurement is less reliable (SOGC 388). From about 9 to 10 weeks fetal movements make accurate measurement harder, and repeat measurements varied more as the CRL grew (Robinson 1975). The CRL is reduced in trisomy 18 and triploidy: do not normalise the findings by redating a fetus with obvious structural anomalies, and take care when the CRL is smaller than expected from an earlier scan (ISUOG 2023). Against Daya's IVF data, Robinson 1975 gave a lower age early in the first trimester and a higher age towards its end; the two agreed for a CRL of 40 to 60 mm (Daya 1993). ISUOG 2023 recommends recent, international, prescriptive charts over older charts.
    6. Source. ISUOG 2023, p. 129-130, Figure 1a, p. 129, and Table 1, p. 130; SOGC 388, Recommendations 2 and 3, p. 1498, p. 1500 and 1502, Table 2, p. 1501; Daya 1993, Methods, p. 904; p. 905, and Table III, p. 906; Robinson 1975, p. 703-706 and 708; Committee Opinion 700, p. e151.

    Embryo age at transfer

    EDD = transfer date + 261 days for a day-5 embryo, or + 263 days for a day-3 embryo (Committee Opinion 700, p. e151).

    Binocular distance

    —

    Enter the BD, 15 to 65 mm.

    From the BPD plane, slide toward the face until both orbits look the same size and each is at its widest; calipers on the outer margin of each eye (orbit), outer to outer (Jeanty 1984, Methods, p. 241; Figure 1, p. 242). Article

    How each paper measured it
    CRL

    Longest straight line from the outer edge of the head to the rump, with the neck in a neutral position. Use the best measurement or the average of several good ones (SOGC 388, Table 2, p. 1501). Calipers placed on the frozen image; Daya averaged two to three measurements, with the fetus extended where possible (Daya 1993, Methods, p. 904).

    When

    Use the earliest first-trimester scan with a CRL of at least 10 mm (about 7 weeks). Use CRL up to 84 mm; above 84 mm, date from the BPD (SOGC 388, Recommendations 2 and 3).

    BPD

    Axial section of the head at the level of the cavum septi pellucidi (Hadlock 1984, Fig. 1a, p. 498), measured with electronic calipers. The paper does not state where the calipers go; it refers to the authors’ earlier papers for the technique (Methods, p. 497).

    HC

    Same plane as the BPD, traced along the outer perimeter of the skull (Hadlock 1982, p. 650), or calculated as (D1 + D2) × 1.57 (Hadlock 1984, p. 497).

    AC

    Axial section of the abdomen at the umbilical part of the left portal vein, with the stomach in view (Hadlock 1984, Fig. 1b, p. 498).

    FL

    Full length of the femoral shaft between the calipers (Hadlock 1984, Fig. 1c, p. 498).

    When

    In the second and third trimesters, date from several biometric parameters rather than one. If dates rest on a third-trimester scan, check interval growth 2 to 3 weeks later (SOGC 388, Recommendations 4 and 5).

    IVF

    After assisted reproduction, the ART-derived gestational age should be used to assign the EDD: from the embryo age and the transfer date (Committee Opinion 700, Recommendations and p. e151). SOGC 388 calculates the EDD from the fertilization date (p. 1502).

    Formula

    Due date

    Source. The gestational age at the exam from the dating result; the redating limits from Committee Opinion 700, Table 1 (p. e152).
    How it is calculated. EDD = exam date + (280 days − gestational age in days). GA today = GA at the exam + days since the exam. The due date calculator uses the same 280 days: GA on a date = 280 − (EDD − date) in days; date for a GA = EDD − (280 − GA in days); LMP-equivalent date = EDD − 280 days. With an LMP entered (CRL and biometry only): GA by LMP = exam date − LMP, EDD by LMP = LMP + 280 days, and the difference = GA by ultrasound − GA by LMP, in days. The difference is compared with the Table 1 limit for the band of GA by LMP; a difference of more than the limit is shown as supporting redating.

    Binocular distance, Jeanty 1984

    Source. Table 2 (p. 242): gestational age at the 5th, 50th and 95th centiles for each whole millimetre of BD, 15 to 65 mm. Table 1 (p. 242): SD of the age estimate by BD band: below 25 mm 0.7 weeks, below 35 mm 0.9, below 45 mm 1.2, below 55 mm 1.5, below 65 mm 2.0.
    How it is calculated. Table 2 values as printed, interpolated linearly between whole millimetres and shown to the nearest day. A second range is calculated here from the Table 1 SD for the BD entered: 50th ± 1.645 × SD (5th to 95th); a BD of exactly 65 mm takes the last band, 2.0 weeks.
    Caution. The Table 2 5th and 95th columns sit about 3.3 weeks either side at every BD, which matches a constant SD of 2.0 weeks; Table 1 gives narrower SDs below a BD of 55 mm. Both ranges are shown.

    About these charts
    • Daya 1993. 94 singleton IVF pregnancies, Hamilton, Ontario, with age known from the day of oocyte retrieval (counted as day 14). Patients had one to three scans; one per pregnancy, chosen at random, was analysed (p. 903-904). CRL 2 to 80 mm (Tables II and III, p. 905-906).
    • Daya's Table II prints 78.6 days for a CRL of 45 mm, the same as for 44 mm. The paper's equation gives 79.3 days and its Table III gives 11.3 weeks (79.1 days), so the printed value is a misprint. The tool uses the equation, which matches the rest of Table II within a quarter of a day.
    • The range shown with Daya is the paper's 95% prediction interval for a single pregnancy (Table III, p. 906), about ±5 days.
    • Robinson 1975. 334 CRL measurements from patients certain of their last period, 6+2 to 14+0 weeks, on a Diasonograph NE4102 (p. 703, 706). A single measurement dates the pregnancy within ±4.7 days with 95% confidence, and within ±2.7 days when three independent measurements are averaged (p. 706).
    • SOGC 388: first-trimester CRL is the best parameter for dating (Recommendation 1). With timed fertilization (assisted reproduction), the due date should come from the fertilization date (p. 1502).
    • Redating, Committee Opinion 700. With an LMP entered, the tool compares the two datings against Table 1 (p. e152), banded by gestational age from the LMP: by CRL, redate when they differ by more than 5 days up to 8+6 weeks and more than 7 days from 9+0 to 13+6 weeks. Smaller differences may still justify a change, depending on how early the scan was and how reliable the LMP is (p. e151). After IVF, the EDD comes from the embryo age and transfer date: 261 days after a day-5 transfer, 263 days after a day-3 transfer (p. e151).
    • Committee Opinion 700. If the pregnancy resulted from assisted reproduction, the ART-derived gestational age should be used to assign the EDD. For in vitro fertilization, the EDD is assigned from the embryo age and the transfer date: 261 days after transfer of a day-5 embryo, 263 days after a day-3 embryo (p. e150-e151).
    • The tool shows the matching gestational age on the transfer day: 2+5 weeks for a day-5 embryo and 2+3 weeks for a day-3 embryo (280 minus 261 or 263 days).
    • Hadlock 1984. 361 singleton fetuses with certain menstrual dates, Houston, each scanned once between 14 and 42 weeks (p. 497-498). Table I gives a regression equation for every combination of BPD, HC, AC and FL; the range shown is ±2 SD for the age band of the estimate (Table II, p. 499).
    • Combining parameters narrows the error, with little gain beyond three (SOGC 388, p. 1502). Uncertainty widens with gestation: ±2 SD is 1.0 to 1.7 weeks before 18 weeks and 2.3 to 3.2 weeks after 36 weeks (Hadlock 1984, Table II).
    • Hadlock 1982. Head circumference alone, 400 fetuses, 15 to 41 weeks (p. 649-650). Listed in the table under the result, for comparison, for HC 80 to 360 mm, the range of Table 3; SD 1.18 weeks (Table 3, p. 651).
    • SOGC 388: up to 23 weeks, second-trimester dating has a 95% interval under one week, close to first-trimester dating. In the third trimester the interval is 2 to 2.4 weeks (p. 1502-1503).
    • Redating, Committee Opinion 700. With an LMP entered, the tool compares the two datings against Table 1 (p. e152), banded by gestational age from the LMP: by biometry, redate when they differ by more than 7 days at 14+0 to 15+6 weeks, 10 days at 16+0 to 21+6, 14 days at 22+0 to 27+6 and 21 days from 28+0. A pregnancy without an ultrasound that confirms or revises the EDD before 22+0 weeks is suboptimally dated (p. e150).

    Fetal biometry

    Centiles for BPD, HC, AC, FL and OFD at the gestational age in the bar above. Enter the full set, or choose one measurement. Tap i beside a measurement for how to take it.

    Chart

    Measurements

    Leave a field blank to skip it. The line under each measurement follows the chart chosen above, because caliper placement differs between charts.

    How each paper measured it
    Formula

    Also entered

    Copied
    About these charts
    • Hadlock 1984. 361 singleton fetuses with certain menstrual dates, Houston, each scanned once (p. 497-498). Mean size for age with a constant SD: BPD 3 mm, HC 1 cm, AC 1.34 cm, FL 3 mm (Table III and footnotes, p. 500). Covers 12 to 40 weeks.
    • BPD and HC use the Table III footnote equations, which reproduce the table within 1 mm either way (rounding). For AC the printed table runs 0 to 1.7 mm above its own footnote equation, and for FL up to 0.8 mm below it between 30 and 36 weeks (up to 0.9 mm at 38 to 39 weeks), so the tool uses the AC and FL columns of Table III, interpolated by day.
    • INTERGROWTH-21st. 4,321 low-risk pregnancies at eight urban sites in eight countries, dated by certain LMP confirmed by CRL, scanned every 5 weeks from 14 weeks (p. 869-871). Mean and SD equations, Table 2, p. 876; centile tables in the web appendix. Covers 14+0 to 40+0 weeks.
    • INTERGROWTH-21st HC and AC were calculated from the two measured diameters with an exact ellipse formula (web appendix, Appendix I); values from a machine's ellipse tool may differ slightly. The formula as printed is missing the π in front of d2.
    • Jeanty 1984. 46 fetuses followed longitudinally by one operator, Brussels (p. 118-119). Reports the 5th, 50th and 95th centiles with a constant SD (Tables 1 and 2, p. 123; Table 3, p. 124), so the tool shows position against those lines and a z score, not an exact centile. BPD measured outer edge to inner edge (p. 127). Its head perimeter is calculated as (BPD + OFD) × 1.62, not traced, and does not match its own BPD and OFD lines (Table 3).
    References
    1. Hadlock FP, Deter RL, Harrist RB, Park SK. Estimating fetal age: computer-assisted analysis of multiple fetal growth parameters. Radiology 1984;152:497-501. Article
    2. Papageorghiou AT, Ohuma EO, Altman DG, et al. International standards for fetal growth based on serial ultrasound measurements: the Fetal Growth Longitudinal Study of the INTERGROWTH-21st Project. Lancet 2014;384:869-879. Article · Web appendix
    3. Jeanty P, Cousaert E, Hobbins JC, Tack B, Bracken M, Cantraine F. A longitudinal study of fetal head biometry. Am J Perinatol 1984;1:118-128. Article
    4. Salomon LJ, Alfirevic Z, Berghella V, et al. ISUOG Practice Guidelines (updated): performance of the routine mid-trimester fetal ultrasound scan. Ultrasound Obstet Gynecol 2022;59:840-856. Article

    Estimated fetal weight

    Centile for gestational age on an in utero ultrasound standard. Choose how the weight is obtained: from biometry with a Hadlock 1985 formula, from the abdominal wall defect formula, or an EFW already calculated.

    Fetal weight

    Hadlock 1985 formula

    HC, AC and FL is the formula the authors suggest for general use and the one SOGC 442 recommends; when a measurement cannot be obtained, choose the formula for the measurements you have (Hadlock 1985, p. 337).

    Same axial view of the head as the HC.

    Same view as the BPD; ellipse on the outer border of the skull.

    1. Plane. The BPD plane.
    2. Landmarks. Both hemispheres symmetrical; the midline echo (falx) broken in front only by the cavum septi pellucidi; thalami on either side of the midline; cerebellum not seen. For INTERGROWTH-21st, the head oval, central and filling at least 30% of the screen.
    3. Calipers. Ellipse placed around the outer border of the skull bone. If the machine has no ellipse, Hadlock 1984 used (D1 + D2) × 1.57 from two diameters at right angles.
    4. Result. Used in the Hadlock 1985 weight formulas; SOGC 442 recommends the HC, AC and FL formula (Recommendation 8).
    5. Pitfalls. The HC is more reliable than the BPD when the head shape is unusual.
    6. Source. ISUOG 2022, p. 843; Hadlock 1984, Methods, p. 497, and Figure 1a, p. 498.

    Transverse abdomen as round as possible; umbilical vein at the portal sinus, stomach seen, kidneys not seen; ellipse on the skin.

    1. Plane. Transverse section of the abdomen, as round as possible, the spine at 3 or 9 o’clock.
    2. Landmarks. Umbilical vein in the front third of the abdomen at the level of the portal sinus (the umbilical part of the left portal vein); stomach seen; kidneys not seen (and, for INTERGROWTH-21st, bladder not seen). For INTERGROWTH-21st, the abdomen filling at least 30% of the screen.
    3. Calipers. Ellipse on the outer surface of the skin. Or two diameters at right angles, both on the outer borders of the body: anteroposterior, from the skin over the spine to the front abdominal wall, and transverse, at the widest point; AC = 1.57 × (AP + transverse).
    4. Result. Used in the Hadlock 1985 weight formulas; SOGC 442 recommends the HC, AC and FL formula (Recommendation 8).
    5. Pitfalls. Too much probe pressure distorts the round shape.
    6. Source. ISUOG 2022, p. 843-844; Hadlock 1984, Figure 1b, p. 498; Papageorghiou 2014, p. 871.

    Femur nearer the probe, close to horizontal, both ends of the shaft seen; calipers on the ends of the ossified shaft.

    1. Plane. Long view of the femur nearer the probe, as close to horizontal as possible. ISUOG: an angle of insonation of 45 to 90 degrees is typical; INTERGROWTH-21st used about 90 degrees with the femur filling at least 30% of the screen.
    2. Landmarks. Both ends of the ossified diaphysis, not hidden by shadows from the adjacent bones.
    3. Calipers. On the ends of the ossified diaphysis, along its longest axis (outer to outer for INTERGROWTH-21st). Leave out the distal femoral epiphysis, the trochanter and pointed spur artefacts at the ends.
    4. Result. Used in the Hadlock 1985 weight formulas; SOGC 442 recommends the HC, AC and FL formula (Recommendation 8).
    5. Pitfalls. Spurs lengthen the bone falsely.
    6. Source. ISUOG 2022, p. 844; Papageorghiou 2014, p. 871; Hadlock 1984, Figure 1c, p. 498.
    EFW (Hadlock HC, AC, FL)—

    Gastroschisis or omphalocele, where the AC is not reliable. Siemer 2008 formula from BPD, OFD and FL.

    Siemer 2008 measured it by the Kurmanavicius 1999 technique and does not describe caliper placement (p. 398).

    EFW (Siemer, BPD, OFD, FL)—

    An EFW already calculated, in grams; the centile is read from Hadlock 1991.

    How the paper measured it
    HC

    Axial section of the fetal head at the level used for the BPD, with the cavum septi pellucidi as the landmark.

    AC

    Axial section of the fetal abdomen showing the umbilical portion of the left portal vein and the stomach. If traced from two perpendicular diameters: (D1 + D2) × 1.57.

    FL

    Section showing the full length of the femur, measured between electronic calipers.

    Hadlock 1984, Fig. 1 and Methods, p. 498. Open the paper

    Abdominal wall defect formula: Siemer 2008 measured BPD, OFD and FL by the techniques of Kurmanavicius 1999 and does not describe caliper placement (p. 398).

    Formula

    EFW, Hadlock 1985

    Source. Hadlock 1985, Table II (p. 334): four regression equations from 276 fetuses (the original 167 and a prospective 109). The authors suggest the HC, AC and FL equation for general use, and a formula chosen from the measurements available when one cannot be obtained (p. 337). SOGC 442 recommends the HC, AC and FL formula (Recommendation 8).
    How it is calculated. Measurements are entered in mm and converted to cm. EFW (g) is calculated with the chosen equation as printed:
    HC, AC, FL: log10 EFW = 1.326 − 0.00326·AC·FL + 0.0107·HC + 0.0438·AC + 0.158·FL
    BPD, HC, AC, FL: log10 EFW = 1.3596 − 0.00386·AC·FL + 0.0064·HC + 0.00061·BPD·AC + 0.0424·AC + 0.174·FL
    BPD, AC, FL: log10 EFW = 1.335 − 0.0034·AC·FL + 0.0316·BPD + 0.0457·AC + 0.1623·FL
    AC, FL: log10 EFW = 1.304 + 0.05281·AC + 0.1938·FL − 0.004·AC·FL
    Caution. In the 276 fetuses the four equations estimated birth weight with an SD of 7.4% (BPD, HC, AC, FL) to 8.0% (AC, FL) (Table III, p. 335). The authors note that differences in population or technique may change the best equation or its coefficients (p. 337).

    Hadlock 1985, Table II, p. 334; Table III, p. 335; p. 337. SOGC Guideline No. 442, Recommendation 8.

    EFW, abdominal wall defect, Siemer 2008

    Source. Siemer 2008: weight formula from BPD, OFD and FL (p. 399), derived in 380 preterm singletons without anomalies delivered at 24+0 to 37+0 weeks (p. 397-398); measurements in cm, EFW in g (p. 398).
    How it is calculated. BPD, OFD and FL are entered in mm and converted to cm. EFW (g) is calculated with the formula as printed:
    EFW = −145.577 + 23.724·FL² + 1.255·BPD³ + 0.001·eOFD − 0.0000406·10FL + 1.03·eFL
    The centile is then read from the Hadlock 1991 standard, as for any EFW.
    Caution. No weight is given before 24+0 weeks: the formula was derived in fetuses delivered at 24+0 to 37+0 weeks (p. 397; Table 2, p. 399). Above an FL of 73 mm the formula’s estimate falls as FL increases, so no weight is given. No weight is given after 37+0 weeks, the end of the derivation group.

    Siemer 2008, p. 397-399. Measurements in cm, EFW in g (p. 398).

    Centile, Hadlock 1991

    Source. Hadlock 1991: 392 fetuses with certain menstrual dates, each scanned once between 10 and 41 weeks (p. 129-130). Equation for the median weight by menstrual age (p. 131). Table 1 (p. 130) prints the 3rd, 10th, 50th, 90th and 97th centiles for each week from 10 to 40 weeks.
    How the lines are calculated. Median (g) from the equation as printed, GA in weeks:
    ln EFW = 0.578 + 0.332·GA − 0.00354·GA²
    The 3rd, 10th, 90th and 97th lines are the median × 0.75, 0.83, 1.17 and 1.25; these reproduce every row of Table 1 within 2 g. The exact centile is read between the printed lines, so a weight on a printed line reads as that centile. Used from 10+0 to 41+0 weeks.
    Not used. A single spread of 13% of the median (p. 132; 12.7% in the abstract), because it does not reproduce the printed lines: a weight on the printed 10th line would read as the 9.5th centile. Table 1 prints the 97th centile at 30 weeks as 1,649 g, a misprint for 1,949 g (median 1,559 g × 1.25).
    Caution. No 5th or 95th line is printed, so none is drawn. No result after 41+0 weeks.

    Hadlock 1991, p. 129-130; Table 1, p. 130; p. 131-132.

    EFW · Hadlock 1991 (the only chart in the library)

    50th 10th, 90th 3rd, 97th This fetus Earlier scans (entered in Growth restriction check)
    Centile line at 32+33rd10th50th90th97th
    About this standard
    • 392 singleton fetuses with certain menstrual dates, each scanned once between 10 and 41 weeks (Hadlock 1991, p. 129-130).
    • The centile lines are those of Table 1 (p. 130): the 3rd, 10th, 90th and 97th are the median × 0.75, 0.83, 1.17 and 1.25. The paper prints no 5th or 95th line.
    • Table 1 prints the 97th centile at 30 weeks as 1,649 g, a misprint for 1,949 g (median 1,559 g × 1.25).
    • The authors suggest the 3rd and 97th centiles as the limits of normal growth, and stress that menstrual age must be known with certainty (p. 133).
    • SOGC 442 recommends plotting EFW on an ultrasound-based fetal growth chart rather than a birth weight chart (Recommendation 9).
    About the abdominal wall defect formula
    • Derived in 380 preterm singletons without anomalies, Erlangen, 2003 to 2006, delivered at 24+0 to 37+0 weeks (median 35+1), scanned within 7 days of birth; birth weight 420 to 3,650 g. Abdominal measurements were not used (p. 397-398). R² 0.873; mean (SD) percentage error 0.44 (11.89), mean absolute percentage error 8.98 (p. 399).
    • Tested in 97 fetuses with an abdominal wall defect (70 gastroschisis, 27 omphalocele), four German centres, 1994 to 2007, delivered at 26+0 to 39+4 weeks, birth weight 750 to 3,380 g. Mean (SD) percentage error −0.84 (12.03), mean absolute percentage error 9.29 (p. 399).
    • In the 67 of these fetuses with an AC, mean (SD) percentage error was −1.77 (11.67) with this formula and −11.02 (12.09) with Hadlock 1985 BPD, HC, AC, FL (not the HC, AC, FL formula used above); 95% limits of agreement with birth weight were −564 to 440 g and −821 to 301 g (Tables 3 and 4, p. 399).
    • No weight is given before 24+0 weeks, the start of the derivation range (24+0 to 37+0 weeks, p. 397). Above an FL of 73 mm the formula's estimate falls as FL increases, so no weight is given. No weight is given after 37+0 weeks, the end of the derivation group.
    • The centile is read from the Hadlock 1991 standard, as for any EFW.

    Growth restriction check

    Fetal growth restriction, early (before 32+0 weeks) or late (32+0 weeks and after), by the Delphi consensus criteria (Gordijn 2016) as adopted by SOGC Guideline No. 442, and small for gestational age by SOGC 442. Values typed here also fill Biometry, Estimated fetal weight and Doppler, and values typed there show here.

    #WeeksDaysEFW, gAC, mm

    Centile over time · EFW (Hadlock 1991) and AC

    Copied
    About these criteria
    • Early FGR, before 32+0 weeks. AC or EFW below the 3rd centile, or absent end-diastolic flow in the umbilical artery; or AC or EFW below the 10th centile combined with a uterine artery PI and/or umbilical artery PI above the 95th centile (Gordijn 2016, Table 6, p. 338). SOGC 442 also counts reversed end-diastolic flow (Box 1, p. 7).
    • Late FGR, 32+0 weeks and after. AC or EFW below the 3rd centile; or at least two of three: AC or EFW below the 10th centile; AC or EFW crossing centiles by more than two quartiles; CPR below the 5th centile or umbilical artery PI above the 95th centile (Gordijn 2016, Table 6, p. 338; SOGC 442, Box 1, p. 7). Absent or reversed end-diastolic flow, when recorded, is counted here as UA-PI above the 95th centile; the late criteria do not list it separately.
    • Crossing centiles. Counted as a fall across two of the 75th, 50th and 25th centile lines between an earlier scan and this one, on the same chart (SOGC 442 gives a drop from the 80th to the 25th centile as an example, p. 7). The growth centiles are non-customised (Gordijn 2016, Table 6 footnote).
    • SGA. AC or EFW below the 10th centile (SOGC 442, Summary statement 2, p. 2); shown here only when the FGR criteria are not met.
    • Congenital anomalies. The definitions apply in the absence of congenital anomalies (Gordijn 2016, Table 6).
    • Charts. EFW is graded on Hadlock 1991. AC and the Doppler values are graded on the chart chosen in Fetal biometry and Doppler (Hadlock 1984 AC, Acharya 2005 UA-PI, Ebbing 2007 CPR and Gómez 2008 uterine artery by default). Jeanty 1984 has no AC chart, so with it chosen in Fetal biometry the AC is not graded.
    • Not part of the definition. MCA-PI alone, ductus venosus, amniotic fluid, customised or conditional centiles, and biomarkers were rejected by the panel (Gordijn 2016, Table 4, p. 337).
    References
    • Gordijn SJ, Beune IM, Thilaganathan B, Papageorghiou A, Baschat AA, Baker PN, Silver RM, Wynia K, Ganzevoort W. Consensus definition of fetal growth restriction: a Delphi procedure. Ultrasound Obstet Gynecol 2016;48:333-339. doi:10.1002/uog.15884 Article
    • Kingdom J, Ashwal E, Lausman A, Liauw J, Soliman N, Figueiro-Filho E, Nash C, Bujold E, Melamed N. Guideline No. 442: Fetal growth restriction: screening, diagnosis, and management in singleton pregnancies. J Obstet Gynaecol Can 2023;45(10):102154. doi:10.1016/j.jogc.2023.05.022 Article

    Birth weight

    Newborn weight for gestational age at birth, by sex.

    Chart

    Newborn

    +

    Both charts are tabulated by completed week, so 39+2 is read as 39 weeks.

    How to read
    • These are newborn weight charts built from birth registrations, not ultrasound charts. For a fetus, use the estimated fetal weight module (SOGC 442, Recommendation 9).
    • Kramer 2001 also gives the mean and SD for each week; the z score shown is (birth weight − mean) / SD, as defined in the paper. Its centile lines are smoothed separately from the mean and SD, so the two can disagree slightly at the extremes (Methods).
    Formula

    Kramer 2001

    Source. Tables 1 and 2 (p. 3), by sex: 3rd, 5th, 10th, 50th, 90th, 95th and 97th centiles, mean and SD of birth weight for each completed week, 22 to 43 weeks.
    How the lines are calculated. Centiles as printed, for the completed week of birth: gestational age is recorded in completed weeks (Methods, p. 2), so a birth at 39+0 to 39+6 is read on the 39-week row. The days are not used and there is no interpolation. The result is the position between the printed centiles. z = (birth weight − mean) / SD, from the printed mean and SD of that week, as defined in the paper; calculated here.
    Caution. The centiles were smoothed separately from the mean and SD, so the centile position and the z can disagree slightly at the extremes (Methods). At 22 weeks (female) the 95th and 97th are printed as the same value, and at 43 weeks (male) the 3rd centile and mean fall below the 42-week values; shown as printed.

    Kramer 2001, Methods, p. 2; Tables 1 and 2, p. 3.

    Dollberg 2005

    Source. Table 2, p. 313: 1st, 5th, 10th, 50th, 90th, 95th and 99th centiles of birth weight for each completed week of gestational age, 22 to 44 weeks, by sex, calculated directly from the registry data (Statistical analysis, p. 311).
    How the lines are calculated. Centiles as printed, for the completed week of birth: a birth at 39+0 to 39+6 is read on the 39-week row. The days are not used and there is no interpolation. The result is the position between the printed centiles; no z score is given.
    Caution. Many lower centiles are printed as exactly 500 g at 22 to 25 weeks; the authors note that numbers are very small at the lowest gestational ages and that at 22 weeks the 1st, 5th and 10th centiles cannot all be 500 g (Discussion, p. 314). The upper centiles at 29 to 33 weeks are irregular: the 99th jumps at 29 weeks, and the 90th to 99th fall from 32 to 33 weeks in both sexes (Table 2, p. 313). Kramer 2001 attributes a bump in uncorrected upper centiles at 27 to 33 weeks to term births recorded at a preterm gestational age (Results, p. 2). Before 34 weeks, Kramer 2001 is the better choice.

    Dollberg 2005, p. 311; Table 2, p. 313; p. 314. Kramer 2001, Results, p. 2.

    About these charts
    • Kramer 2001. All singleton live births in Canada 1994 to 1996 except Ontario: 347,570 males and 329,035 females, 22 to 43 completed weeks. Births probably misrecorded as preterm when they were term were removed with a mixture model, and the centiles smoothed (Methods, p. 2; Tables 1 and 2, p. 3).
    • Kramer prints the 95th and 97th centiles for females at 22 weeks as the same value (576 g), and at 43 weeks the male 3rd centile and mean fall below the 42-week values (small numbers). Shown as printed.
    • Dollberg 2005. Israeli national birth registry 1993 to 2001, 754,713 singletons (p. 311). Centiles calculated for each completed week, 22 to 44 weeks (1st, 5th, 10th, 50th, 90th, 95th, 99th; p. 311; Table 2, p. 313). Many lower centiles are exactly 500 g at 22 to 25 weeks, and the upper centiles at 29 to 33 weeks are irregular (Table 2; Discussion, p. 314). Before 34 weeks, Kramer 2001 is the better choice.
    References
    1. Kramer MS, Platt RW, Wen SW, et al. A new and improved population-based Canadian reference for birth weight for gestational age. Pediatrics 2001;108(2):e35. Article
    2. Dollberg S, Haklai Z, Mimouni FB, Gorfein I, Gordon ES. Birth weight standards in the live-born population in Israel. Isr Med Assoc J 2005;7:311-314. Article
    3. Kingdom J, Ashwal E, Lausman A, et al. Guideline No. 442: Fetal growth restriction: screening, diagnosis, and management in singleton pregnancies. J Obstet Gynaecol Can 2023;45(10):102154. Article

    Doppler

    Umbilical artery PI, RI and S/D, middle cerebral artery, CPR, uterine artery and MCA peak systolic velocity at the gestational age in the bar above, with a serial check of the umbilical artery against a previous scan.

    Measurements

    CPR is calculated as MCA-PI / UA-PI when both are entered.

    The chart uses the mean PI: enter left and right (the mean is calculated), or the mean PI alone. One side alone gets no centile.

    Previous UA Doppler (serial check)

    The last umbilical artery values of this fetus and the gestational age they were taken, for the Acharya 2005 conditional range. Enter any of PI, RI or S/D.

    Fetal sex for Acharya 2020 CPR only
    How to measure
    UA

    Free-floating loop of cord, fetus quiet, angle under 15° with angle correction if needed, wall filter at its lowest, large gate. Average three consecutive uniform cycles (Acharya 2005, Methods, p. 938).

    RI, S/D

    Read from the same umbilical artery waveforms as the PI: RI = (peak systolic − end-diastolic velocity) / peak systolic velocity; S/D = peak systolic / end-diastolic velocity (Acharya 2005, Methods, p. 938).

    MCA

    Transverse plane lowered from the biometry plane to the base of the brain, just below the thalami, to show the circle of Willis. Gate in the proximal third of the MCA, angle 20° or less, five uniform cycles (Bahlmann 2002, Methods, p. 491).

    CPR

    MCA-PI divided by UA-PI from the same examination (Ebbing 2007, Methods, p. 288).

    UtA

    Transabdominal from 15 weeks: probe in the lower quadrant angled medially, sample about 1 cm beyond the apparent crossing of the external iliac artery. Transvaginal at 11 to 14 weeks, sampled at the cervicocorporeal junction before the artery branches. Angle under 30°, three similar waveforms; left and right PI averaged (Gómez 2008, Methods and Fig. 1, p. 129).

    PSV

    Axial view at the thalami and cavum septi pellucidi; MCA sampled close to its origin from the internal carotid, angle as near 0° as possible, no fetal movement or breathing; take the highest point of the waveform (Mari 2000, Methods, p. 10).

    Formula

    Also entered

    Chart shows
    Chart

    Copied
    About these charts
    • UA-PI, Acharya 2005. 130 low-risk pregnancies, Tromsø, Norway, scanned 3 to 5 times from 19 to 42 weeks; free-loop sampling, one operator (p. 937-938). Centiles from the paper's equations (Appendix, p. 943), which reproduce Table II within 0.012.
    • UA-RI and UA S/D, Acharya 2005. Same cohort and examinations as the UA-PI chart. Centiles from the Appendix equations (p. 944), which reproduce Table III (RI) within 0.005 and Table IV (S/D) within 0.05 (the largest gaps at the 97.5th centile at 19 and 21 weeks; medians within 0.01 except 0.03 at 19 weeks and 0.02 at 21 weeks).
    • Serial check, Acharya 2005. Because each fetus was scanned 3 to 5 times, the paper gives conditional equations (Appendix, p. 943-944): from a previous value, the expected value at the next scan and its 95% range, which the authors consider more appropriate for following an individual fetus (Discussion, p. 942).
    • MCA-PI, Bahlmann 2002. 962 low-risk pregnancies, Mainz, each examined once at 18 to 42 weeks (p. 490-491). Table I gives fitted values (smoothed by nonlinear regression) of the mean and a 90% interval, about the 5th to 95th centiles (p. 492, 495); the tool interpolates by day between weeks, with no result after 42+0, and shows position against those lines. The mean printed for 33 weeks, 1.739, is a misprint for 1.839: the paper's own polynomial (Table III) gives 1.839 and its neighbours agree.
    • MCA-PI and CPR, Ebbing 2007. 566 observations in 161 low-risk pregnancies, Bergen, Norway, most scanned 3 to 5 times (p. 288-289); the tables give centiles from the fitted multilevel model at each week, 21 to 39 weeks (Tables 3 and 5, p. 290 and 293). The Appendix S1 and S2 equations are not used; the tool interpolates the printed centiles by day between weeks, with no result after 39+0, and shows position between lines.
    • Ciobanu 2019. 72,387 unselected singleton pregnancies, London and Medway, UK, one visit each, at 20+0 to 22+6, 31+0 to 33+6, 35+0 to 36+6 or 41+0 to 41+6 weeks (the curves between these windows are modelled); deliberately includes pregnancies with complications, so it is a reference range rather than a normal range (p. 465-466). Centiles from the supplement equations (Table S1), which reproduce Table 2. Mean z-scores differ slightly by maternal age, BMI, racial origin, conception, smoking, parity and diabetes (Table S3, Figure 3); every group mean lies within 0.17 SD of zero. The tool applies no adjustment.
    • CPR, Acharya 2020. 284 low-risk pregnancies, Bergen and Tromsø, scanned about every 4 weeks; separate tables of centiles from the fitted multilevel model for male, female and both sexes, 19 to 40 weeks (p. 189; Tables 2-4, p. 191-192). Equations are online only, so the tool interpolates the printed centiles by day between weeks, with no result after 40+0. The Bergen data overlap with Ebbing 2007.
    • Uterine artery, Gómez 2008. 620 low-risk singleton pregnancies, Barcelona, 20 per week from 11 to 41 weeks, cross-sectional; transvaginal at 11 to 14 weeks and transabdominal after (p. 128-129). Centiles from the paper's equation with gestational age in days (Results, p. 130).
    • MCA-PSV, Ebbing 2007. Same Bergen cohort as the MCA-PI chart; Table 2 (p. 290) prints PSV centiles from the fitted model for each week, 21 to 39 weeks; no result after 39+0. None of the fetuses was at risk of anaemia (Methods, p. 288). Offered beside Mari 2000 as a normal range; the paper gives no anaemia thresholds.
    • MCA-PSV, Mari 2000. Median = e2.31 + 0.046 × GA (Methods, p. 10). In 111 fetuses at risk from red-cell alloimmunisation, 1.50 MoM detected all moderate and severe anaemia without hydrops, with a 12% false-positive rate (p. 10-11). The printed equation runs up to 1 cm/s below the Table 3 median and up to 1.5 cm/s below the Table 3 1.50 and 1.55 MoM values near term; the tool uses the equation. Table 3 ends at 40 weeks, so there is no result after 40+0.
    References
    1. Acharya G, Wilsgaard T, Berntsen GKR, Maltau JM, Kiserud T. Reference ranges for serial measurements of umbilical artery Doppler indices in the second half of pregnancy. Am J Obstet Gynecol 2005;192:937-944. Article
    2. Bahlmann F, Reinhard I, Krummenauer F, Neubert S, Macchiella D, Wellek S. Blood flow velocity waveforms of the fetal middle cerebral artery in a normal population: reference values from 18 weeks to 42 weeks of gestation. J Perinat Med 2002;30:490-501. Article

    Amniotic fluid

    Three ways to measure amniotic fluid. Choose the one you measured; each has its own chart.

    Measurements

    Amniotic fluid index largest pocket per quadrant, cm

    AFI is the sum of the quadrants when they are entered; otherwise enter it directly.

    Abdomen in four quadrants; depth of the largest pocket in each, added. Before 20 weeks Magann 2000 used the two lower quadrants only.

    1. Plane. The abdomen divided into four quadrants (Magann 2000).
    2. Calipers. Depth of the largest pocket in each quadrant; the AFI is the sum of the four. Before 20 weeks the study used the right and left lower quadrants only.
    3. Result. Position against the Magann 2000 centiles for gestational age, with the normal range, and the fixed cut-offs used in the paper: 5 cm or less (oligohydramnios) and above 24 cm (hydramnios).
    4. Pitfalls. In the Magann 2000 cohort of normal pregnancies, an AFI of 5 cm or less labelled 8% as oligohydramnios, against 1% for the deepest pocket. For an AFI of 5 cm, the 95% range of dye-dilution volumes was 91 to 1026 mL (a study cited by Magann 2000). SOGC 2017 recommends a single pocket estimate for the first assessment on a routine scan.
    5. Source. Magann 2000, Methods, p. 1582; p. 1581-1582 and 1586; SOGC 2017 No. 340, p. 53.

    Find the single largest pocket first; measure its depth. SOGC 2017 (Chamberlain): depth at right angles to the uterus, pocket at least 1 cm wide.

    1. Plane. Identify the single largest pocket of fluid first (Magann 2000).
    2. Calipers. Depth of the pocket. The Chamberlain method, which SOGC 2017 advocates: depth measured at right angles to the uterus, in a pocket at least 1 cm wide.
    3. Result. Position against the Magann 2000 centiles, with the normal range, and the fixed cut-offs: below 2 cm and above 8 cm (Magann 2000; Chamberlain, SOGC 2017).
    4. Pitfalls. Techniques vary: some operators accept any 2 by 1 cm pocket whatever the probe angle, and others hold the probe vertical, parallel to the maternal sagittal plane. Maternal position and probe orientation are usually not described in the literature.
    5. Source. Magann 2000, Methods, p. 1582; SOGC 2017 No. 340, p. 53, 55 and 56.

    Width of the same single largest pocket, for the 2-diameter pocket.

    1. Calipers. Width of the same pocket used for the deepest pocket depth (Magann 2000).
    2. Source. Magann 2000, Methods, p. 1582.

    Depth multiplied by width of the single largest pocket; calculated here when both are entered.

    1. Calipers. No separate calipers: 2-diameter pocket = depth × width of the single largest pocket (Magann 2000).
    2. Result. Position against the Magann 2000 centiles, with the normal range, and the fixed cut-offs: below 15 cm² and above 50 cm².
    3. Pitfalls. In the Magann 2000 cohort of normal pregnancies, below 15 cm² labelled 30% as oligohydramnios, against 1% for the deepest pocket.
    4. Source. Magann 2000, Methods, p. 1582; p. 1581-1582.

    2-diameter pocket = depth × width of the single largest pocket.

    How the paper measured it
    SDP

    Find the single largest pocket of fluid first and measure its depth (Magann 2000, Methods, p. 1582).

    2DP

    Multiply the depth of that same largest pocket by its width (Magann 2000, Methods, p. 1582).

    AFI

    Divide the abdomen into four quadrants, measure the largest pocket in each and add the four. Before 20 weeks the study used the right and left lower quadrants only (Magann 2000, Methods, p. 1582).

    Formula

    Also entered

    Copied
    About these charts
    • Magann 2000. 1,400 low-risk singleton pregnancies, Jackson, Mississippi; 50 patients at each week from 14 to 41 weeks, each scanned once. Exclusions: medical or obstetric complications, birth weight below the 10th or above the 90th centile, 5-minute Apgar below 7 (p. 1581-1582). 57% of the cohort was African American (p. 1582).
    • Tables I to III give the 5th, 10th, 50th, 90th and 95th centiles predicted by polynomial regression for each week from 14 to 41 weeks (Methods, p. 1582; p. 1584-1585). Centile lines between weeks are interpolated linearly by day from these weekly values; there is no result after 41+0. The tool shows position between the printed lines, not an exact centile. The figure-legend equations are rounded too far to reproduce the tables and are not used.
    • AFI at 17 weeks: the printed 10th centile, 4.0 cm, is below the printed 5th centile, 4.1 cm. The tool uses 4.6 cm, the midpoint of the 16- and 18-week 10th centiles.
    • Fixed cut-offs are the definitions used in the paper: oligohydramnios AFI 5 cm or less, deepest pocket below 2 cm, 2-diameter pocket below 15 cm²; hydramnios AFI above 24 cm, deepest pocket above 8 cm, 2-diameter pocket above 50 cm² (p. 1581-1582). In this cohort these labelled 8%, 1% and 30% as oligohydramnios, and 0%, 0.7% and 3% as hydramnios. The cut-offs are shown only from 14+0 to 41+0 weeks, the range of the cohort.
    • The authors provided normative data for 14 to 41 weeks but did not establish what thresholds should be used to consider a value abnormal (Comment, p. 1587).
    References
    1. Magann EF, Sanderson M, Martin JN, Chauhan S. The amniotic fluid index, single deepest pocket, and two-diameter pocket in normal human pregnancy. Am J Obstet Gynecol 2000;182:1581-1588. doi:10.1067/mob.2000.107325 Article
    2. Lim KI, Butt K, Naud K, Smithies M. Amniotic fluid: technical update on physiology and measurement. SOGC Technical Update No. 340. J Obstet Gynaecol Can 2017;39(1):52-58. Article

            Measurements

            Lung volume and pulmonary hypoplasia

            FLB

            3D volume of the whole thorax from a transverse plane at the four-chamber view, heart nearest the probe. Outline each lung in the transverse plane six times, rotating 30° each time (rotational method); right plus left lung = total lung volume. EFW by Hadlock from BPD, HC, AC and FL (Ruano 2006, Methods, p. 959, Figure 1).

            MRI

            Total fetal lung volume is outlined on T2-weighted MRI. Enter the observed volume in mL from the MRI report, and the O/E is calculated here from the Meyers 2018 formula for the gestational age in the bar above; or enter the O/E percentage from the MRI report (for example 45, not 0.45) (Mehollin-Ray 2024, Methods and Figure 1, p. 44-45; Meyers 2018, Methods, p. 433-434).

            Formula
            Fetal lung-to-body weight (FLB) ratio, Ruano 2006.
            Source. Methods (p. 959): FLB ratio = total lung volume on 3D ultrasound (mL) / estimated fetal weight (g), with pulmonary hypoplasia defined by the autopsy cut-offs, below 0.015 before 28 weeks and below 0.012 from 28 weeks. Results (p. 958, 960): with these cut-offs, the ultrasound FLB ratio detected 11 of 12 fetuses with pulmonary hypoplasia at autopsy (sensitivity 91.7%, specificity 91.3%).
            How it is calculated. FLB ratio = lung volume / EFW, calculated here, compared with the cut-off for the gestational age in the bar above. No cut-off is applied outside 15+0 to 38+6, the weeks the paper studied.
            Caution. 35 fetuses scanned just before termination of pregnancy for fetal anomalies, 15 to 38 weeks, one operator (p. 959); lung volume is taken as equal to lung weight (1 mL = 1 g).

            Ruano 2006, Methods, p. 959; Results, p. 960; Abstract, p. 958.

            MRI O/E total fetal lung volume in skeletal dysplasia, Mehollin-Ray 2024; expected volume, Meyers 2018.
            Source. Mehollin-Ray 2024, Table 2 (p. 45): lethality (stillbirth or death in the first month) in 80 fetuses with skeletal dysplasia: O/E below 49%, sensitivity 0.63, specificity 0.93, positive predictive value 0.94, negative predictive value 0.59 (AUC 0.81); O/E below 38%, sensitivity 0.47, specificity 1.00, positive predictive value 1.00, negative predictive value 0.52. Methods (p. 44): the O/E was calculated with the Meyers formula for expected total fetal lung volume for gestational age. Meyers 2018, Results (p. 435): expected total fetal lung volume (mL) = 0.000865 × GA3.254, GA in weeks (R² 0.8368), from 665 fetuses with MRI at 18 to 38 weeks.
            How it is calculated. When the observed total fetal lung volume (mL) from the MRI report is entered, the expected volume is calculated here at the gestational age in the bar above, by day, for 18+0 to 38+6, the weeks Meyers 2018 studied, and O/E = observed / expected × 100. Otherwise the O/E percentage from the MRI report is used. The O/E is placed against the two cut-offs for MRI at 18+0 to 36+6, the weeks Mehollin-Ray 2024 studied. The paper writes the cut-offs as fractions (0.49 and 0.38); an entered O/E of 1 or less is taken as a fraction and not graded, so enter it as a percentage.
            Not used. Meyers 2018 Table 3 (p. 436), the formula’s values at whole weeks: the formula reproduces them within 0.06 mL from 18 to 38 weeks, so it is evaluated directly. The measured weekly means of Meyers 2018 Table 1 (p. 434), which Meyers proposes for counselling in the second trimester (p. 437): Mehollin-Ray 2024 used the formula.
            Caution. Skeletal dysplasia only; MRI at 18 to 36 weeks; lethal fetuses were imaged earlier (mean 25.8 against 29.8 weeks, Table 1, p. 45). Meyers 2018 had only 16, 9 and 2 fetuses at 36, 37 and 38 weeks, and its measured means at those weeks fall below the formula (for example 85.5 mL against 109.68 mL at 37 weeks; Tables 1 and 3), so an O/E calculated late in pregnancy can read low. Mehollin-Ray 2024 Figure 1 (p. 45) reports 11.43 mL at 23+1 weeks as 47% of expected; the formula at 23+1 gives 23.81 mL, or 48%; the paper does not say how gestational age entered the formula.

            Mehollin-Ray 2024, Methods, p. 44; Figure 1 and Tables 1 and 2, p. 45. Meyers 2018, Table 1, p. 434; Results, p. 435; Table 3, p. 436; Discussion, p. 437.

            References

            2. Mehollin-Ray AR, Stover S, Cassady CI, Zhang B, Calvo-Garcia M, Kline-Fath B. Using MRI-derived observed-to-expected total fetal lung volume to predict lethality in fetal skeletal dysplasia. Pediatr Radiol 2024;54:43-48. doi:10.1007/s00247-023-05825-0 Article
            3. Meyers ML, Garcia JR, Blough KL, Zhang W, Cassady CI, Mehollin-Ray AR. Fetal lung volumes by MRI: normal weekly values from 18 through 38 weeks’ gestation. AJR Am J Roentgenol 2018;211:432-438. doi:10.2214/AJR.17.19469 Article

                    After birth: UTD P1 to P3

                    For the newborn scan, taken more than 48 hours after birth: transverse view at the renal hilum, prone preferred, the same position at each follow-up scan (Nguyen 2014, p. 989-990).

                    Other findings
                    Formula
                    Source. Table 3 (p. 989): normal values after 48 hours of life (APRPD below 10 mm, no calyceal dilation, normal parenchyma, ureters and bladder). Text (p. 990) and Figure 6 (p. 993): UTD P1, P2 and P3. Recommendation 4 (p. 991-992): follow-up for each class.
                    How it is calculated. The class is set by the most concerning finding. P3: abnormal parenchymal thickness or appearance, or an abnormal bladder, whatever the APRPD. P2: APRPD 15 mm or more, peripheral calyceal dilation, or a dilated ureter. P1: APRPD 10 to under 15 mm, or central calyceal dilation. Otherwise, with an APRPD below 10 mm, within the normal values of Table 3. No calculation beyond these rules.
